Adjusted take using the August 2021 Beige Book: The FOMC’s September 22 statement notes strengthening activity and employment with risks from the Delta wave and elevated (largely transitory) inflation, and signals that tapering may soon be warranted. The Beige Book published in August 2021 corroborates ongoing expansion but at a more moderate pace due to Delta-related headwinds, widespread labor shortages, rising wages, elevated prices, and persistent supply-chain constraints across districts (including New York). These conditions validate the Fed’s emphasis on risks to the outlook and elevated inflation, even as overall financial conditions remain accommodative. While the July SLOOS points to firmer credit demand and easing terms—supporting a “taper soon” trajectory—the Beige Book’s moderation and labor/supply frictions temper the positivity. Net effect: moderately positive, but a notch below the SLOOS-only read.
